business_model: On-demand home cleaning marketplace, low fixed price point, independent-contractor labor

historical_evidence.company: Founded by Adora Cheung and Aaron Cheung, a Y Combinator graduate offering on-demand home cleaning bookable online.
historical_evidence.market: Large, highly fragmented home-cleaning services market with no dominant national brand as of 2013, a genuinely large addressable wedge for a marketplace model.
historical_evidence.team: Y Combinator pedigree; founders had operated the business since a 2012 YC batch, giving roughly 18 months of operating history by the snapshot date.
historical_evidence.product: Simple, low-friction online booking for home cleaning at a flat, aggressively low price point (reported around $20/hour) — a clear, easy-to-understand consumer product with low onboarding friction.
historical_evidence.execution: Progressed from a small 2012 seed round to a combined $38M Series A/B in December 2013 led by Google Ventures (with Redpoint Ventures, Max Levchin, and First Round Capital also participating) in roughly 18 months — a fast, well-backed fundraising trajectory with blue-chip investor participation.
historical_evidence.traction: Operating in 31 cities as of the snapshot per contemporaneous coverage; no specific repeat-customer, retention, or unit-volume figures were found in the sources reviewed.
historical_evidence.financial: The stated $20/hour price point was widely discussed in coverage as aggressive relative to the cost of sourcing, vetting, and retaining independent-contractor cleaners at scale, though no specific contemporaneous unit-economics figures (contractor pay, customer acquisition cost) were found in the sources reviewed for this snapshot — flagged as a real, evidence-visible-in-principle risk rather than a hindsight-informed one, since the tension between a low flat price and a fragmented, quality-variable contractor labor pool was an inherent, observable feature of the business model at the time, independent of what happened later.
